newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Bid clears future for Swedish glassmaker.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Bid clears future for Swedish glassmaker.

text.p: Sweden's most famous glassmaker, Orrefors Kosta Boda, will stay under Swedish control after rival suitors buried the hatchet with a joint takeover bid on Tuesday.

Swedish heckles were raised early this month when Danish luxury goods maker Royal Copenhagen appeared poised to make a move on the prestigious, designer glassmaker and Swedish investment group Proventus AB put up a fight.

On Tuesday, Royal Copenhagen, Proventus and an investment arm of third major shareholder, Investor AB, put forward a joint takeover bid as a compromise to all parties involved that was hoped to appease national ire.
"It upset many people that a foreign company could take control," Proventus managing director Mikael Kamras told Reuters.

"It is such an old company with so many very nice traditions and such a strong brand name that is clearly connected with the Swedish heritage," Kamaras said of the glassmaker, which was formed in 1990 by the merger of rivals Orrefors and Kosta Boda. Orrefors and Kosta Boda trademarks remain separate.

The row over Orrefors Kosta Boda began early this month when Denmark's silver, porcelain and glass maker Royal Copenhagen, which is 82 percent owned by Danish brewer Carlsberg AS, lifted its stake to 17 percent.

Proventus, which is owned 91.5 percnt owned by Swedish financier Robert Weil, responded by increasing its stake to 21 percent with an option for a further 9.1 percent and making a bid at 145 crowns a share for up to 20 percent of equity.
Meanwhile, during the battle for control, the 23.1-percent holding by Investor, the investment vehicle of Sweden's Wallenberg business empire, remained unknown.

But last Friday, the three companies announced they were locked in talks over future ownership of Orrefors Kosta Boda and on Tuesday, came to the market with news of a joint takeover bid, offering 155 crowns per share.

The bid was made by a consortium of Proventus, Royal Copenhagen, and investment group Scandinavian Equity Partners Ltd (SEP). SEP is owned 46 percent by Investor, 21 percent by S-E-Banken, 21 percent by U.S. private investment company AEA Investors Inc and the rest by management.
"The deal needed some diplomacy," SEP spokesman Conni Jonsson told Reuters following the announcement.
Investor said it was positive about the bid and will put its holding into the consortium while Proventus withdrew its earlier offer for shares.
Kamras said the cooperation with Royal Copenhagen was important for the future of the prestigious glass company.
He said the agreement built on an arrangement between the Danish group and Orrefors Kosta Boda made in July this year for cooperation on marketing and sales in overseas markets.
"The important thing for Orrefors Kosta Boda is to increase sales outside Sweden, and we have to cooperate with someone at least at the beginning of this process," Kamras said.

The takeover bid, open from November 18 to December 6, will leave Proventus with a 42.5-percent stake of Orrefors Kosta Boda, SEP with 42.5 percent and Royal Copenhagen with 15 percent. The consortium already controls 73.9 percent.
Orrefors Kosta Boda shares closed 12 crowns higher at 152 crowns on news of the takeover bid.
